title: feat(auth): flag-gated passkey and magic-link login entry points
body:
## Context

`GET /api/v1/auth/config` advertises two login-surface capability flags that this
repository declares but never consumes: `features.passkeys` and `features.magicLink`
(`packages/auth/src/types.ts`). objectui#2514 established that fact and — per the
maintainer's 2026-08-03 ruling on that card — closed the honesty gap by documenting both
flags as **reserved / not consumed**, deliberately deferring the UI:

> 选 **2（摘牌/文档化）**：短期把 `passkeys` / `magicLink` 在文档标注 **reserved**，不建 UI；登录面 UI 进产品路线，有档期再做（届时按 flag 驱动渲染）。

This card is the deferred half — the UI itself. It is filed **unqueued and unassigned**
for the maintainer's roadmap call: building it stays one decision away, honestly labeled,
rather than implied by a flag that does nothing.

## Scope

Two independent, flag-gated entry points on the login surface. Each renders **only** when
the server advertises the corresponding flag, exactly as `features.sso`,
`features.phoneNumberOtp` and `features.deviceAuthorization` already gate theirs — an
entry point that can only fail at click time is the failure mode all of those exist to
avoid.

### 1. Passkeys — gated on `features.passkeys === true`

- `LoginForm` shows a "sign in with a passkey" entry point.
- Registration / management of a passkey for the signed-in user (account security surface).
- Client API: better-auth's passkey plugin, registered in `createAuthClient.ts` alongside
  the existing `organizationClient()` and `twoFactorClient()`.
- WebAuthn availability is a second gate on top of the flag: the browser may not support
  it, so the entry point degrades to nothing rather than to an error.

### 2. Magic link — gated on `features.magicLink === true`

- `LoginForm` shows an "email me a sign-in link" mode beside the password form.
- Request step (submit the address) and consume step (the route the emailed link lands on,
  exchanging the token for a session).
- Client API: better-auth's magicLink plugin.

### Out of scope

- `features.twoFactor` — deliberately not read by `LoginForm`; the 2FA challenge is driven
  by server-side remediation (framework ADR-0069). Unlike the two flags above, the 2FA
  capability is already implemented in this repo (`createAuthClient`'s `enableTwoFactor` /
  `verifyTwoFactor`), so it is a different case entirely and not part of this card.
- Whether the framework should keep advertising the two flags at all
  (`packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts`, whose `exempt.reason` points at
  objectui#2514) — that is the framework lane's call, not this repo's.

## Acceptance criteria

- Neither entry point renders when its flag is absent or falsy. That is today's behaviour
  and it must survive as the default.
- Both entry points render, and complete a real sign-in, when the flag is true.
- The reserved markings retire **together with** the implementation: the "reserved" doc
  comments on the two declarations, the reserved subsection in `packages/auth/README.md`,
  and the pin test `packages/auth/src/__tests__/reserved-auth-features.test.ts` are all
  deleted in the same PR that lands the first consumer. The pin's own docblock says so, and
  the pin fails the moment a consumer appears without that cleanup.
- i18n keys for every new user-facing string; a changeset.

## References

- objectui#2514 — the reserved-flag documentation (Option 2, landed)
- framework#2874 P2② — the login-surface audit this came out of
